attack: Recipient substituted in the quoted requirements
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: detectable (PAYMENT_REQUIREMENTS_MISMATCH). To notice, a verifier needs the payee allowlist, which the receipt does not carry.

attack: Atomic amount substituted in the quoted requirements
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: detectable (PAYMENT_REQUIREMENTS_MISMATCH). To notice, a verifier needs the requirements actually served, to compare against payment_requirements_hash.

attack: F-1. Declared asset precision rescales the decimal amount
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: still not detectable. To notice, a verifier needs independent knowledge of the asset's true precision, which appears nowhere in the receipt.

attack: F-4. Signed authorisation diverges from the accepted requirements
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: still not detectable. To notice, a verifier needs the payload itself, to recompute the payload hash and inspect the inner authorisation.

attack: F-7. Scheme named in the receipt was never evaluated
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: detectable (PAYMENT_REQUIREMENTS_MISMATCH). To notice, a verifier needs the requirements actually served — scheme is inside payment_requirements_hash, so a substitution is caught, though the receipt still cannot show the field was never evaluated.

attack: F-7. Agent named in the receipt was never evaluated
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: still not detectable. To notice, a verifier needs the policy source, to learn that evaluatePolicy never reads agent_id.

attack: F-7. Requirement timeout bound into the hash but never compared to expiry
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: detectable (PAYMENT_REQUIREMENTS_MISMATCH). To notice, a verifier needs the requirements actually served — the value is inside payment_requirements_hash even though it is not surfaced as a receipt field.

attack: F-7. Authorisation validity window never compared to decision expiry
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: still not detectable. To notice, a verifier needs the payload, to read validBefore and compare it to expires_at.

attack: F-5. Principal chosen by the caller, keying the cumulative budget
expectation: A verifier holding only the receipt should be able to tell that a policy-bearing value was substituted.
observed: receipt-only verification: valid, substitution NOT detectable. With the served requirements supplied: still not detectable. To notice, a verifier needs the credential-to-tenancy mapping, which is not modelled anywhere.

attack: F-7. Telling from the receipt alone which bound fields were actually evaluated
expectation: A receipt should let a verifier distinguish a field the issuer checked from one it merely copied.
observed: A signed ALLOW carrying scheme=deferred, agent_id=agent_impostor, maxTimeoutSeconds=86400 and an authorisation whose validBefore is in the past verifies cleanly. Its reason codes — MERCHANT_ALLOWED, WITHIN_TRANSACTION_LIMIT, WITHIN_DAILY_LIMIT — name no field, so nothing in the receipt distinguishes an evaluated field from a copied one. Substitution of scheme or maxTimeoutSeconds is separately detectable to a verifier holding the served requirements, because both sit inside payment_requirements_hash; that detects a changed value, not an unchecked one.

attack: F-6. Distinguishing a derived receipt from a caller-asserted one, offline
expectation: A verifier should be able to tell whether the issuer derived the facts it signed or accepted them from the caller.
observed: A decision produced through InntrisX402Guard.authorise and one produced by handing provider.evaluate a caller-authored action are field-identical once the per-issuance values are removed, and both verify. inntris-decision-v1 carries no provenance or derivation-path field, so the distinction is not recoverable from the receipt.
